learningObjectives.title: The nature and features of the Church

questions.q: According to the Nicene Creed, what are the four traditional marks (notes) of the Church?
questions.explain: The Nicene Creed describes the Church as 'one, holy, catholic and apostolic', which are called the four marks of the Church.

questions.q: Which image does St Paul use to describe the Church as a single community with Christ as its head?
questions.explain: St Paul teaches that the Church is the 'Body of Christ', with each believer a part of one body united in Christ.

questions.q: In the phrase 'one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church', what does the word 'catholic' mean?
questions.explain: Here 'catholic' means universal, showing the Church is for all people everywhere, not a single nation or group.

questions.q: Why is the Church described as 'apostolic'?
options: Its faith and mission are founded on the teaching of the apostles
It was built entirely in the twentieth century
It rejects the authority of Scripture
It only exists in the city of Rome
questions.explain: 'Apostolic' means the Church continues the faith, teaching and mission handed down from the apostles.

questions.q: How many sacraments does the Catholic Church recognise?
questions.explain: The Catholic Church recognises seven sacraments, including Baptism, Confirmation and the Eucharist.

questions.q: How many sacraments do most Protestant churches recognise?
questions.explain: Most Protestant churches recognise two sacraments because they see only these two as clearly instituted by Jesus in the Gospels.

questions.q: Which two sacraments are accepted by most Protestant churches?
options: Anointing of the Sick and Confirmation
questions.explain: Most Protestants accept Baptism and Holy Communion (the Lord's Supper) as the two sacraments commanded by Jesus.

questions.q: What does the Catholic doctrine of transubstantiation teach about the Eucharist?
options: The bread and wine become the body and blood of Christ
The bread and wine are only ever plain symbols
The bread and wine are removed from the service
The bread and wine represent the Ten Commandments
questions.explain: Transubstantiation is the Catholic belief that at the consecration the bread and wine truly become the body and blood of Christ.

questions.q: Which Catholic sacrament of initiation strengthens and completes the grace of Baptism, often involving anointing with oil by a bishop?
questions.explain: Confirmation is a sacrament of initiation in which a person is strengthened in faith, usually through anointing by a bishop.

questions.q: What best describes liturgical worship?
options: Worship that follows a set structure or order of service
Worship that has no plan and is entirely spontaneous
Worship carried out alone at home
Worship that never uses the Bible
questions.explain: Liturgical worship follows a fixed order or pattern, such as the structure of the Catholic Mass.

questions.q: Which statement best describes non-liturgical worship?
options: It does not follow a fixed set order and can be more flexible
It must always be led by the Pope
It can only take place in a cathedral
questions.explain: Non-liturgical worship has no set liturgy and is often more informal and flexible in structure.

questions.q: Believer's baptism, carried out on adults by full immersion in water, is especially associated with which type of church?
questions.explain: Baptist churches practise believer's baptism, baptising those old enough to make their own faith commitment, usually by full immersion.

questions.q: A Catholic feels guilty about something wrong they have done and wants to confess their sins to a priest and receive absolution. Which sacrament are they seeking?
questions.explain: The sacrament of Reconciliation (Penance/Confession) allows a person to confess sins and receive God's forgiveness through the priest.

questions.q: Who is the head of the Catholic Church on earth?
options: The Moderator of the General Assembly
questions.explain: The Pope is the visible head of the Catholic Church and is regarded as the successor of St Peter.

questions.q: What is meant by apostolic succession?
options: The unbroken line of authority passed from the apostles down through the bishops
The idea that only women may lead worship
The belief that the Bible was written by the Pope
The practice of baptising only adults
questions.explain: Apostolic succession is the belief that authority has been handed down in an unbroken line from the apostles to today's bishops.

questions.q: The Pope is also known as the Bishop of which city?
questions.explain: The Pope is the Bishop of Rome, the office traditionally traced back to St Peter.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key role of a Catholic priest in parish life?
options: Celebrating Mass and administering the sacraments
Writing new books of the Bible
questions.explain: A priest leads worship, celebrates Mass and administers the sacraments while serving the local parish community.

questions.q: A local church organises a food bank, visits the sick and raises money for the poor. Which aspect of Christian life does this best show?
options: Community life expressed through service and charity
The four marks of the Church
questions.explain: Serving the needy through charity and outreach is a key expression of Christian community life.

questions.q: A Christian says, 'The Church is for people of every nation and race, not just one country.' Which mark of the Church is this expressing?
questions.explain: Saying the Church welcomes all nations reflects the mark 'catholic', meaning universal.

questions.q: A congregation follows a printed order of service with set prayers and responses each week. This is an example of which kind of worship?
questions.explain: A fixed order of service with set prayers and responses is a feature of liturgical worship.
